Acetyl hexapeptide-3 (widely known as [Argireline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acetyl_hexapeptide-8) and now scientifically reclassified as **acetyl hexapeptide-8** ) is `a synthetic anti-aging peptide used in topical serums and creams to help smooth expression lines and wrinkles`.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acetyl_hexapeptide-8)[[2]](https://www.instagram.com/reel/C56EBQuOTOW/?hl=en)[[3]](https://stonevillenc.org/argireline--acetyl-hexapeptide-3--clear/)

### How It Works

- **Botox-like effect:** It mimics a portion of the SNAP-25 protein to destabilize the SNARE complex, which stops neurons from releasing neurotransmitters that cause facial muscles to contract.[[1]](https://cellbone.com/pages/acetyl-hexapeptide-3argireline%C2%AE)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acetyl_hexapeptide-8)[[3]](https://sincereskincare.com/ingredients/acetyl-hexapeptide-3/)
- **Muscle relaxation:** By easing repeated muscle tension around the forehead, eyes, and mouth, it softens dynamic wrinkles like crow's feet and frown lines.[[1]](https://www.specialchem.com/cosmetics/product/spec-chem-industry-argireline-acetyl-hexapeptide-3-solution)[[2]](https://www.instagram.com/reel/C56EBQuOTOW/?hl=en)[[3]](https://hzrebtech.com/product/0-05-acetylhexapeptide-3-solution/)
- **Non-invasive alternative:** Unlike injectable neurotoxins, it is applied topically, requires no needles or prescriptions, and works gently on the skin's surface.[[1]](https://www.instagram.com/reel/C56EBQuOTOW/?hl=en)[[2]](https://hzrebtech.com/product/0-05-acetylhexapeptide-3-solution/)

### Benefits and Uses

- **Reduces wrinkle depth:** Clinical studies show regular use helps diminish the depth of expression lines.[[1]](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/Acetyl-hexapeptide-3)[[2]](https://www.specialchem.com/cosmetics/product/spec-chem-industry-argireline-acetyl-hexapeptide-3-solution)[[3]](https://hzrebtech.com/product/0-05-acetylhexapeptide-3-solution/)
- **Improves firmness:** It encourages a tighter, firmer look and supports skin mechanical properties.[[1]](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/299591539_Acetyl_hexapeptide-3_in_a_cosmetic_formulation_acts_on_skin_mechanical_properties_-_Clinical_study)[[2]](https://hzrebtech.com/product/0-05-acetylhexapeptide-3-solution/)
- **Common formulations:** Found typically in 5% to 10% concentrations inside water-based face serums, anti-aging gels, and spot-treatment creams.[[1]](https://inkeedecoder.com/ingredients/acetyl-octapeptide-3)[[2]](https://www.specialchem.com/cosmetics/product/spec-chem-industry-argireline-acetyl-hexapeptide-3-solution)
- **Nomenclature note:** If you see "acetyl hexapeptide-3" or "acetyl hexapeptide-8" on an ingredient label, you are looking at the exact same active cosmetic molecule.[[1]](https://stonevillenc.org/argireline--acetyl-hexapeptide-3--clear/)

- What other **active ingredients** (like retinol or vitamin C) are currently in your routine?
